Fill in suppressed county counts

Source: R/impute_suppressed.R
impute_suppressed.Rd

CDC suppresses small county counts. impute_suppressed() gives each suppressed county a count so county data can be added up or shared across census tracts with extrapolate_from_county(). Run it on county data from get_atlas() before no_county_cases() or extrapolate_from_county().

Rows are handled by what CDC published:

  • A published count is kept, whatever its data status. (Connecticut's 2017 planning regions are marked "Data not available" but have counts.)

  • A row marked "Data not available" with no count has no data to estimate from; not_available says whether it is dropped or kept. Either way its cases are still in the state total, so no_county_cases() counts them in the remainder.

  • Any other row with no count is suppressed and is filled in by method.

Usage

impute_suppressed(
  x,
  method = c("state_rate", "zero"),
  cap = 4,
  floor = 0,
  population = c("cdc", "acs"),
  unestimated = c("na", "zero"),
  not_available = c("drop", "keep")
)

Arguments

x

County data from get_atlas(geography = "county").

method

How suppressed counts are filled in:

  • "state_rate" (default): the state's rate in the same indicator, year and stratum, times the county's population (see population), kept between floor and cap.

  • "zero": 0. Useful as a sensitivity analysis.

cap

The largest count "state_rate" can give a suppressed county. Use Inf for no cap. The default, 4, reflects CDC suppressing counts of 1 to 4, but complementary suppression can hide larger counts, so it is a default rather than a hard limit.

floor

The smallest count "state_rate" can give. The default, 0, allows for counties suppressed because their population is under 100, which may have no cases. Use 1 to treat every suppressed county as having at least one case. Must not be larger than cap.

population

The county population "state_rate" multiplies by:

  • "cdc" (default): CDC's own county population, the same source as the state rate's denominator.

  • "acs": the county's ACS 5-year population in the same stratum and ages, summed from its tracts as extrapolate_from_county() does. Needs tidycensus and a Census API key.

Neither covers Connecticut's 2017 planning regions: CDC gives them no population, and 2017 ACS tracts belong to the old counties (#30).

unestimated

What to do with a suppressed row "state_rate" can't estimate, because the state rate or county population is missing:

  • "na" (default): leave it NA, with a warning. no_county_cases() counts its cases in the remainder with no county, and extrapolate_from_county() leaves it out (or stops, with unestimated = "error").

  • "zero": set it to 0, with a warning.

not_available

Rows marked "Data not available" with no count:

  • "drop" (default): remove them, with a message.

  • "keep": keep them with NA cases. The later steps leave them out.

Value

x with suppressed counts filled in and a new column cases_source:

  • "published": CDC's count.

  • "state_rate" or "zero": filled in by method.

  • "not estimated": "state_rate" couldn't estimate it; NA, or 0 with unestimated = "zero".

  • "not available": kept with not_available = "keep"; NA.

data_status is unchanged, so suppressed rows can still be identified. cap, floor, population and unestimated apply only to "state_rate".

Details

"state_rate" downloads the state data matching x (same diseases, years and stratification) from CDC AtlasPlus, and with population = "acs" the tract populations from the Census.

See also

no_county_cases() for cases in state totals that no county accounts for; extrapolate_from_county() for the next step.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
county <- get_atlas("hiv", "county", 2022, stratify_by = "sex")
county <- impute_suppressed(county)

# Sensitivity analysis: suppressed counties have no cases
county_zero <- impute_suppressed(
  get_atlas("hiv", "county", 2022, stratify_by = "sex"),
  method = "zero"
)
} # }
